merged as 1d358fb. THE ORIGINAL FIX WAS ITSELF BROKEN and the gate caught it: gpu_timing.rs set destination_offset = range.start * 8, but wgpu-types-0.20.0/src/lib.rs:80 defines QUERY_RESOLVE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT = 256 and wgpu-core-0.21.1 command/query.rs:423 enforces it, while the resolve buffer is only 144 bytes - so 0 was the ONLY legal destination_offset and no positional offset could ever be valid. Three unit tests asserted the illegal values 16/48/128, locking it in. Latent only because engine_demo shipped one scene with all 9 passes on. FIX: each written run resolves to offset 0 of a scratch buffer, then copy_buffer_to_buffer to a positional readback slot (COPY_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT 4; every readback offset is first_pass*16; max end 144 = exactly the buffer size). Safety comes from wgpu-core's tracker emitting a real pipeline barrier (query.rs:504, transfer.rs:735), NOT from encoder ordering - documented in the code because a future reader who believed the ordering story could batch the resolves and lose it silently. The 'write all 9' alternative was correctly REJECTED: a pass that never executes cannot write its slots, so resolving them is the original unreset-slot UB. GUARD: alignment_guard sweeps all 2^9 masks against the re-exported wgpu constant, seen FAILING first ('emits resolve destination_offset 16 which is not a multiple of 256'). ACCEPTANCE CRITERION MET FOR THE FIRST TIME, on real hardware, verified independently by the gate: RX 7800 XT with ssao disabled, pre-fix EXIT=101 'Resolve buffer offset has to be aligned', post-fix EXIT=0, 8 passes, ssao correctly absent.
